record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Ergodicity for the three-parameter Volterra family
record.original_question: Consider the Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on S^2 defined by x' = x(1 + ay - bz), y' = y(1 - ax + cz), and z' = z(1 + bx - cy), with a, b, c in [-1, 1]. The known result states that when a, b, and c are all nonzero and have the same sign, the Cesaro averages (1/n) sum_{k=0}^{n-1} V^k(x) fail to converge for this operator. Determine the exact role of this parameter condition for the ergodic theorem: in particular, is the stated condition sufficient to decide when the ergodic theorem holds or fails for this family?

evidence.quote: V : S2 → S2  x′ = x (1 + ay − bz) , y ′ = y (1 − ax + cz) , z ′ = z (1 + bx − cy) , where a, b, c ∈ [−1, 1].
Theorem 3. [3] If the parameters a, b, c for the Volterra QSO (9) have the same sign and each is non-zero, then the ergodic theorem will fail for this operator.
Problem 4. Is the condition of Theorem 3 sufficient for the ergodic theorem to hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let S^2 = {(x,y,z) ∈ ℝ^3 : x,y,z ≥ 0, x+y+z = 1} denote the two-dimensional standard simplex. For parameters a, b, c ∈ [−1, 1], define the Volterra quadratic stochastic operator V : S^2 → S^2 by
  x' = x(1 + ay − bz),
  y' = y(1 − ax + cz),
  z' = z(1 + bx − cy).
Say that the ergodic theorem holds for V if, for every initial point x ∈ S^2, the Cesàro averages
  A_n(x) = (1/n) ∑_{k=0}^{n−1} V^k(x)
converge as n → ∞. It is known that whenever a, b, c are all nonzero and all have the same sign, the ergodic theorem fails for V (i.e. there exists x ∈ S^2 for which A_n(x) does not converge).

Question: Is the condition "a, b, c are all nonzero and have the same sign" also necessary for the failure of the ergodic theorem? Equivalently, does the ergodic theorem hold for V for every choice of (a,b,c) ∈ [−1,1]^3 not satisfying this condition (i.e. when at least one of a,b,c is zero, or when they do not all share the same sign)?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed the ergodicity of Volterra quadratic stochastic operators on the two-dimensional simplex. In particular, a 2012 preprint claims to give a full description of the ergodic properties of three-dimensional Volterra QSOs, and a 2025 chapter "Ergodic Volterra Quadratic Mappings of the Simplex" presents a complete analysis of asymptotic behavior on the three-dimensional simplex, which would resolve the question of necessity for this three-parameter family. However, since I could not directly verify a precise statement matching the claimed converse, the status is recorded as partially_solved.

status_evidence.snippet: a Volterra quadratic stochastic operators of three dimensional simplex into itself is considered. The full description of ergodic properties such operators is given.
status_evidence.claim: Claims a complete description of the ergodic properties of Volterra QSOs on the two-dimensional simplex, which would settle whether the sign condition is also necessary.

status_evidence.title: Ergodic Volterra Quadratic Mappings of the Simplex
status_evidence.snippet: A complete analysis of the asymptotic behavior of trajectories of Volterra quadratic mappings of the three-dimensional simplex into itself has been presented.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work claims a complete analysis of asymptotic behavior, relevant to the necessity direction of the ergodic-theorem condition.
